title: Introduce intake metadata canonicalizer and release-notes mosaic generator
author: Maya Chen
body:
Motivation: onboarding pipelines are ingesting model metadata from multiple sources (manual manifests, partner CSVs, third-party registries). We observed drift in canonical fields (alias vs canonical_name, hw_affinity tags, license canonicalization) which causes noisy diffs in changelogs and makes automated release notes brittle. This PR introduces a small, focused intake pipeline component (intake-canonicalizer) that normalizes and fingerprints key metadata fields and a complementary 'release-notes mosaic' generator that aggregates small, per-model deltas into a human-readable mosaic for release drafts.

Goals: 1) Reduce churn in changelogs by normalizing semantically-equivalent metadata variants (e.g. "MIT" vs "MIT License", gpu_affinity vs hw_affinity) prior to profile diffing. 2) Attach an affinity fingerprint to intake manifests so downstream variant selection and scheduling hints are stable. 3) Produce compact release-note mosaics that group small metadata-only changes across many models into a single digestible section for release managers.

What changed (high level): - New module: services/intake/canonicalizer.py and CLI wrapper tools/bin/intake-normalize. The canonicalizer implements rule-based normalization + a compact deterministic hashing strategy for canonical keys. - New module: tools/release/mosaic_builder.py which consumes normalized intake snapshots and compact per-model deltas to assemble a multi-model mosaic summary (with provenance links). - Onboard hook: a lightweight preflight hook was added to the intake HTTP handler (api/intake/handler.py) to run canonicalization and attach metadata_fingerprint. - Tests: unit tests and a small integration test that runs a representative CSV -> intake -> registry flow. - Docs: docs/onboard/canonicalization.md and a usage example in quickstarts/onboard-mosaic-example.md.

Checklist: - [x] Canonicalization rules implemented for name, license, tags, and hw_affinity. - [x] Deterministic fingerprint algorithm documented and tested. - [x] Release mosaic generator produces grouped human-readable summary for UI and email drafts. - [x] CI integration (unit + smoke) passing. - [x] Backwards-compatible: existing registry records keep original raw_manifest field for audit.

Usage notes: After deployment, existing intake items will be backfilled by a one-off job (scripts/backfill/normalize_snapshots.py). New intake submissions will receive a metadata_fingerprint in the registry response. The mosaic generator is available as tools/release/mosaic_builder.py --input <delta-dir> --output mosaic.md and emits links to intake snapshots for each tile.

Related work and constraints: This design intentionally keeps canonicalization rule-based and deterministic instead of using an ML normalizer to keep transparency for compliance teams. We avoided touching semver/versioning logic; the mosaic groups metadata-only changes and flags any profile/perf changes for separate rollout notes.

Commits summary:
- a1b3d9f: initial canonicalizer module and simple rule set
- b27f4c2: add CLI + ingestion hook, attach metadata_fingerprint
- c8d1aee: mosaic_builder and presentation renderer (markdown + json-lines)
- d4f87bc: tests, docs, and backfill script
- e5a09db: fix edge cases for empty-affinity tags and add CI flakiness guard

Changed areas (high-level paths):
- services/intake/canonicalizer.py
- tools/release/mosaic_builder.py
- api/intake/handler.py (preflight hook)
- scripts/backfill/normalize_snapshots.py
- docs/onboard/canonicalization.md
- quickstarts/onboard-mosaic-example.md
- tests/intake/test_canonicalizer.py

Small code example (CLI):
> tools/bin/intake-normalize --source path/to/raw.csv --dry-run

Testing and CI: Unit tests added for canonicalization edge cases (null tags, multi-aliases) and deterministic fingerprinting. CI matrix runs canonicalizer tests on Python 3.10/3.11, quick smoke integration on a small local sqlite registry. The mosaic generation step is covered by an integration test that asserts grouping behavior for 50 synthetic deltas.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature flag intakes.canonicalize.enabled = false. 2) Enable for 10% of new intakes and run the backfill job in parallel. 3) Monitor registries and release-mosaic output for diffs for two weeks. 4) Ramp to 100% and deprecate legacy post-processing that attempted to merge aliases.

Open questions: - Should we add a mapping table for corporate-partner license synonyms beyond the current compact heuristics? (follow-up ENG-3241) - Do we want to extend the mosaic renderer to produce structured release note objects for the Release Notes API? (PM follow-up)

This PR is intended to be low-risk and reversible: the canonicalizer writes normalized fields to a separate canonical_manifest and preserves raw_manifest for audits. The mosaic generator is an off-line tool and does not change registry state.

review_conversation: Ethan Rivera: Nice clean separation. One question: how do we avoid collisions in metadata_fingerprint for multi-tenant hosts? Suggest we prefix by tenant id in the hash domain.
Maya Chen: Good point — updated the canonicalizer to include tenant_id salt when present; added tests.
Priya Nair: Will the canonicalizer cause unexpected churn in existing downstream release automation? We should ensure the mosaic only consumes canonical_manifest when feature flag is on.
Maya Chen: Mosaic reads from diffs produced by the reconcile pipeline which respects the feature flag. Added explicit guard in mosaic_builder to ignore canonicalized-only deltas unless flag is set.
Luca Moretti: Small nit: prefer shorter fingerprint (10 bytes) for human-friendly URLs. Is there risk to collision?
Maya Chen: We keep a 16-byte truncated blake2b by default; exposed as config to shrink to 10 bytes with a warning in docs.
release_notes: Adds an intake canonicalizer that normalizes model metadata and attaches a deterministic metadata_fingerprint; introduces a release-notes mosaic generator to group metadata-only deltas into compact release summaries. Backfill script provided. Config flag guards rollout.
